subsections: Central Legislative Assembly elections under the 1919 Act

accepted.s: The first elections to the Central Legislative Assembly under the Government of India Act, 1919, were held in:
accepted.x: The first elections under the 1919 constitutional arrangements were held in 1920. The Congress boycotted these elections.
accepted.tq: Use the exact year rather than confusing the first election with the later Swarajist contest.
accepted.sec: Central Legislative Assembly elections under the 1919 Act  [other exams]

accepted.s: The principal objective of the Swaraj Party in contesting the elections of 1923 was to:
o: Obstruct the working of the legislatures from within
Accept the reforms and cooperate with the government
Demand immediate partition of British India
accepted.x: The Swaraj Party, led by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru, entered the legislatures in order to obstruct colonial governance from within.
accepted.tq: Identify the political purpose behind entering the legislatures instead of merely recalling the party name.
accepted.sec: Central Legislative Assembly elections under the 1919 Act  [other exams]

accepted.s: With reference to the Swarajists in the elections of 1923, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: They won about 10 per cent of the seats and rejected legislative politics.
They won about 25 per cent of the seats and formed the government at the Centre.
They won about 40 per cent of the seats and demanded a review of the 1919 Act.
They won a majority of all provincial seats and abolished dyarchy.
accepted.x: The Swarajists secured about 40 per cent of the seats in 1923 and demanded a review of the Government of India Act, 1919.
accepted.tq: Split the option into the seat share and the associated demand; both details must match.
accepted.sec: Central Legislative Assembly elections under the 1919 Act  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Muddiman Committee of 1924 was appointed in response to the demand of the Swarajists for:
o: A review of the Government of India Act, 1919
accepted.x: The Muddiman Committee was the British response to the Swarajist demand for a review of the working of the Government of India Act, 1919.
accepted.tq: Link the committee to the demand that caused its appointment.
accepted.sec: Central Legislative Assembly elections under the 1919 Act  [other exams]

accepted.s: Who became the President, or Speaker, of the Central Legislative Assembly after the Swarajist success in 1923?
accepted.x: Vithalbhai Patel became the President, commonly described as the Speaker, of the Central Legislative Assembly.
accepted.tq: Use the office-holder trap by distinguishing the legislative leaders from the presiding officer.
accepted.sec: Central Legislative Assembly elections under the 1919 Act  [other exams]

accepted.s: V. Ramadas was elected to the Central Legislative Assembly from Andhra in:
accepted.x: V. Ramadas was elected to the Central Legislative Assembly in 1923.
accepted.tq: Recall the regional candidate together with the election year.
accepted.sec: Central Legislative Assembly elections under the 1919 Act  [other exams]

accepted.s: The elections to the provincial legislatures held in 1937 were followed by which of the following developments?
o: The Congress won in the provinces, while the Centre continued under the 1919 structure.
The federation under the 1935 Act came into operation immediately.
The Swaraj Party returned to the legislatures for the first time.
accepted.x: The Congress won in the 1937 provincial elections. The Centre continued under the 1919 structure because the proposed federation never came into existence.
accepted.tq: Test the comparison between provincial implementation and the unformed federal Centre.
accepted.sec: Central Legislative Assembly elections under the 1919 Act  [other exams]

accepted.s: The immediate political pressure that prompted the Montagu Declaration of 20 August 1917 was exerted chiefly by the:
accepted.x: The Home Rule Leagues created political pressure that contributed to the British declaration recognising self-government as an objective.
accepted.tq: Identify the immediate political force rather than the later constitutional outcome.
accepted.sec: Montagu Declaration 1917  [other exams]

accepted.s: Montagu and Chelmsford toured India in December 1917 primarily to:
o: Consult Indian opinion on constitutional reforms
Conduct elections to the Central Legislative Assembly
accepted.x: Montagu and Chelmsford toured India in December 1917 as part of the process of consulting Indian opinion on constitutional reforms.
accepted.tq: Match the tour with its constitutional-reform context, not with later events.
accepted.sec: Montagu Declaration 1917  [other exams]

accepted.s: A 27-member Andhra delegation led by Nyapati Subbarao met Montagu at Madras to demand:
o: A separate Muslim province in South India
Abolition of the Madras Legislative Council
accepted.x: The Andhra delegation led by Nyapati Subbarao sought the creation of a separate Andhra province.
accepted.tq: Connect the delegation leader and its regional constitutional demand.
accepted.sec: Montagu Declaration 1917  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the response of the Moderates to the constitutional reforms of 1919?
o: They accepted the reforms and formed the Indian National Liberal Federation in 1918.
They boycotted the reforms and formed the Justice Party.
They joined the Home Rule Leagues and demanded complete independence.
They rejected the reforms and formed the Swaraj Party.
accepted.x: Surendranath Banerjee and other Moderates accepted the reforms, left the Congress and formed the Indian National Liberal Federation in 1918.
accepted.tq: Use the founder-group and organisation pairing to avoid confusing Moderates with Swarajists.
accepted.sec: Moderates' exit - Indian National Liberal Federation  [other exams]

accepted.s: At the Amritsar Congress of 1919, the reforms were described as:
accepted.x: The Amritsar Congress characterised the reforms as inadequate, unsatisfactory and disappointing.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact three-part political assessment used by the Congress.
accepted.sec: Moderates' exit - Indian National Liberal Federation  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Andhra reaction to the reforms of 1919:
1. A special Andhra Mahasabha was held at Guntur on 17 August 1918.
2. It was held under the leadership of Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.
3. Krishna Patrika described the reforms as giving with the right hand and taking with the left.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Guntur meeting, its leadership and the Krishna Patrika description reflect the critical Andhra response to the reforms.
accepted.tq: Check the date, regional leader and exact contemporary description together.
accepted.sec: Moderates' exit - Indian National Liberal Federation  [other exams]

accepted.s: The official name of the Rowlatt Act was the:
o: Indian Security and Public Order Act, 1919
accepted.x: The official title of the Rowlatt Act was the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act, 1919.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the popular name from the exact statutory title.
accepted.sec: Rowlatt Act - official name, provisions, Satyagraha

accepted.s: The Rowlatt Act was passed on:
accepted.x: The Rowlatt Act was passed on 10 March 1919. 6 April was the date of the Rowlatt Satyagraha hartal, while 13 April was the date of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
accepted.tq: Separate the dates of enactment, hartal and massacre rather than treating them as one event.
accepted.sec: Rowlatt Act - official name, provisions, Satyagraha

accepted.s:
Which of the following were provisions of the Rowlatt Act?
1. Arrest and detention without warrant or trial
2. In-camera trials by a three-judge High Court panel
3. Right of appeal to the Privy Council in every case
4. Suspension of habeas corpus
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Act permitted arrest and detention without warrant or trial, in-camera trials by a three-judge High Court panel and suspension of habeas corpus. It did not provide an appeal in every case.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong procedural safeguard by testing the exceptional powers against the claimed right of appeal.
accepted.sec: Rowlatt Act - official name, provisions, Satyagraha

accepted.s: The Rowlatt Act came into existence as an extension of the:
accepted.x: The Rowlatt legislation extended the extraordinary powers earlier provided under the Defence of India Act, 1915.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the parent wartime legislation from the later Rowlatt enactment.
accepted.sec: Rowlatt Act - official name, provisions, Satyagraha

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Gandhi's response to the Rowlatt Act?
o: He accepted the Act and entered the Viceroy's Executive Council.
He formed the Indian National Liberal Federation.
He launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1915.
He launched his first all-India campaign through the Rowlatt Satyagraha.
accepted.x: The Rowlatt Satyagraha was Gandhi's first all-India campaign. It was organised through a Satyagraha Sabha and included a hartal on 6 April 1919.
accepted.tq: Identify the movement by its scale and immediate historical context.
accepted.sec: Rowlatt Act - official name, provisions, Satyagraha

accepted.s: The Rowlatt Act was repealed during the viceroyalty of:
accepted.x: The Rowlatt Act was repealed under Lord Reading, along with the Press Act of 1910.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the viceroy associated with repeal from the one in office when the Act was passed.
accepted.sec: Rowlatt Act - official name, provisions, Satyagraha

accepted.s: The statutory review provision of the Government of India Act, 1919 required the appointment of a commission after:
accepted.x: The Act required a statutory commission to review its working after ten years. The Simon Commission was appointed two years early under this provision.
accepted.tq: Recall the statutory interval and distinguish it from the actual early appointment.
accepted.sec: Statutory review clause

accepted.s: The Simon Commission was appointed two years before the statutory review period because it was constituted in:
accepted.x: The Government appointed the Simon Commission in 1927, two years before the ten-year review point prescribed by the 1919 Act.
accepted.tq: Calculate the early appointment against the ten-year review clause.
accepted.sec: Statutory review clause

accepted.s: The Simon Commission was appointed in November 1927 by the:
o: Liberal Government under David Lloyd George
accepted.x: The Simon Commission was appointed in November 1927 by the Conservative Government headed by Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin.
accepted.tq: Match the commission with the government in power at the time of appointment.
accepted.sec: Simon Commission - composition, arrival, boycott and protests  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Simon Commission, consider the following statements:
1. It consisted of seven members.
2. All its members were British.
3. Sir John Simon was its chairman.
4. Clement Attlee was one of its members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The commission had seven members, all British, with Sir John Simon as chairman; Clement Attlee was also a member.
accepted.tq: Verify composition, nationality, chairmanship and membership before selecting the coded option.
accepted.sec: Simon Commission - composition, arrival, boycott and protests  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Simon Commission was also known as the:
o: Indian Statutory Commission or White Commission
accepted.x: The Simon Commission was officially associated with the name Indian Statutory Commission and was popularly called the White Commission because it had no Indian member.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the formal designation from the popular descriptive name.
accepted.sec: Simon Commission - composition, arrival, boycott and protests  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Simon Commission arrived at Bombay on:
accepted.x: The Simon Commission arrived at Bombay on 3 February 1928.
accepted.tq: Separate the appointment year from the year of arrival in India.
accepted.sec: Simon Commission - composition, arrival, boycott and protests  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the correct route of the Simon Commission through Andhra?
accepted.x: The Andhra route of the Simon Commission was Tenali, Guntur, Vijayawada, Ongole and Madras.
accepted.tq: Arrange the places in geographical travel sequence rather than selecting isolated locations.
accepted.sec: Simon Commission - composition, arrival, boycott and protests  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I (Place)
a. Lahore
b. Madras
c. Lucknow
d. Tenali and Guntur
List-II (Protest leader)
i. Tanguturi Prakasam
ii. G.V. Unnayya Sastri
iii. Lala Lajpat Rai
iv. Jawaharlal Nehru and G.B. Pant
accepted.x: Lahore was associated with Lala Lajpat Rai, Madras with Tanguturi Prakasam, Lucknow with Jawaharlal Nehru and G.B. Pant, and Tenali–Guntur with G.V. Unnayya Sastri.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure place–leader pair and eliminate codes containing incompatible matches.
accepted.sec: Simon Commission - composition, arrival, boycott and protests  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Tanguturi Prakasam acquired the title 'Andhra Kesari' in connection with which incident?
o: Baring his chest before the police during the anti-Simon Commission protest at Madras
Leading the Home Rule League in Andhra
Leading the boycott of the Rowlatt Act in Guntur
accepted.x: Tanguturi Prakasam bared his chest before the police during the anti-Simon Commission protest at Madras and became known as Andhra Kesari.
accepted.tq: Link the title to the distinctive action and place associated with it.
accepted.sec: Simon Commission - composition, arrival, boycott and protests  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The lathi charge on Lala Lajpat Rai at Lahore on 30 October 1928 was ordered by:
accepted.x: The lathi charge was ordered by SP James Scott. Saunders, who is sometimes confused with Scott, was later shot by Bhagat Singh and Rajguru in an act of revenge.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the officer who ordered the lathi charge and the officer later targeted in revenge.
accepted.sec: Simon Commission - composition, arrival, boycott and protests  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the anti-Simon Commission organisation in Andhra?
o: G.V. Unnayya Sastri presided over the committee, while M.A. Ansari toured Andhra.
Bulusu Sambamurthy presided over the committee, while S. Satyamurti toured Punjab.
Tanguturi Prakasam presided over the committee, while Lala Lajpat Rai toured Andhra.
S. Satyamurti presided over the Andhra anti-Simon committee, while Bulusu Sambamurthy toured Andhra for the boycott.
accepted.x: S. Satyamurti was president of the Andhra anti-Simon committee, and Bulusu Sambamurthy toured Andhra to promote the boycott.
accepted.tq: Avoid the swapped-person trap by matching each leader with the correct organisational role.
accepted.sec: Simon Commission - composition, arrival, boycott and protests  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following was NOT a recommendation of the Simon Commission Report?
1. Abolition of provincial dyarchy
2. Introduction of provincial autonomy
3. Retention of separate electorates
4. Immediate establishment of a responsible federal government at the Centre
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The report recommended abolition of provincial dyarchy, provincial autonomy and retention of separate electorates. It did not recommend the immediate establishment of a responsible federal government at the Centre.
accepted.tq: Find the one proposal that does not belong among the report's actual recommendations.
accepted.sec: Simon Commission - composition, arrival, boycott and protests  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Simon Commission Report recommended the separation of:
o: Sindh from Bombay and Burma from India
Bihar from Bengal and Assam from India
Burma from Bengal and Orissa from Bihar
Andhra from Madras and Sindh from Punjab
accepted.x: The report recommended separating Sindh from Bombay and Burma from India.
accepted.tq: Use the paired territorial recommendation rather than confusing it with later provincial reorganisation.
accepted.sec: Simon Commission - composition, arrival, boycott and protests  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The term 'Scheduled Castes' was first used in the:
accepted.x: The term 'Scheduled Castes' was first used in the Simon Commission Report.
accepted.tq: Match the exact constitutional term with the report in which it first appeared.
accepted.sec: Simon Commission - composition, arrival, boycott and protests  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following constitutional milestones in chronological order:
A. Nehru Report
B. Partition of Bengal
C. Gandhi-Irwin Pact
D. Jinnah's Fourteen Points
accepted.x: The correct order is Partition of Bengal (1905), Nehru Report (1928), Jinnah's Fourteen Points (1929), and Gandhi-Irwin Pact (March 1931).
accepted.tq: Anchor the earliest and latest milestones first, then place the 1928 and 1929 developments between them.
accepted.sec: Chronology of constitutional milestones  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: 1919 — Government of India Act and Rowlatt Act
accepted.x: The Rowlatt Act and the Government of India Act were both associated with 1919. The Partition of Bengal was in 1905, the Morley-Minto Reforms in 1909 and the Nehru Report in 1928.
accepted.tq: Check each year against the constitutional milestone instead of relying on a familiar title alone.
accepted.sec: Chronology of constitutional milestones  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Nehru Report and Jinnah's Fourteen Points were issued in, respectively:
accepted.x: The Nehru Report was issued in 1928, followed by Jinnah's Fourteen Points in 1929.
accepted.tq: Distinguish two closely spaced constitutional documents by their consecutive years.
accepted.sec: Chronology of constitutional milestones  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was concluded in:
accepted.x: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was concluded in March 1931.
accepted.tq: Use the month and year to distinguish the pact from the Civil Disobedience events surrounding it.
accepted.sec: Chronology of constitutional milestones  [APPSC, GROUP-II]
